column4: A second deposit queued in the same epoch overwrites the first and its funds are unrecoverable
column5: A second deposit queued in the same epoch overwrites the first and its funds are unrecoverable -- ### Summary `Vault.sol:queueDeposit()` writes every incoming request at index 0 of the per-epoch request array instead of appending it at the next free slot, so the second depositor in an epoch silently replaces the first request in place. The replaced depositor's assets have already been pulled in and no record of them survives, so nothing can ever claim them back. ### Root Cause The request index is hardcoded to 0 in the slot preimage instead of being derived from the current queue length.

column4: Redemption rounds in the redeemer's favour because shares are burned before the supply snapshot
column5: Redemption rounds in the redeemer's favour because shares are burned before the supply snapshot -- ### Summary `Vault.sol:redeem()` burns the caller's shares and only then reads `totalSupply()` to compute the assets owed, so the divisor is already smaller than the supply the shares were minted against and every redemption pays out slightly more than the holder's pro-rata claim. Repeated in a loop it drains the rounding difference from the remaining holders. ### Root Cause The supply snapshot is taken after the burn instead of before it.

column4: Epoch settlement prices redemptions off a stale cached oracle reading
column5: Epoch settlement prices redemptions off a stale cached oracle reading -- ### Summary `Vault.sol:settleEpoch()` values the epoch's redemptions with the oracle price cached when the epoch opened rather than refreshing it, so an epoch that stays open across a large price move settles every redemption at the old price and pays the exiting holders out of the remaining ones. ### Root Cause The cached price is never invalidated at settlement time.

column4: Accrued protocol fees are burned when no treasury has been configured
column5: Accrued protocol fees are burned when no treasury has been configured -- ### Summary `Vault.sol:sweepFees()` transfers the accrued protocol fee to the configured treasury without checking that one was ever set, so on a deployment that left the treasury at its default the whole accrued fee balance is sent to the zero address and permanently destroyed. ### Root Cause The recipient is used without a zero-address guard.
